quizName: Hardest Questions in Iowa Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You should skip them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are vulnerable on the road. Always use your turn signals when you change lanes or turn. Use them even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: What is one benefit of a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It does not restrict your side vision.
It can reduce the severity of a head injury.
It is always comfortable to wear.
It makes it easier to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can reduce the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your specific motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your motorcycle. It includes specifications, how to operate it, and maintenance needs.

questions.question: What should you do about checking your mirrors?

options.text: Check them regularly as part of your normal scanning.
Avoid checking them because they distract you.
Skip them because other drivers can see you easily.
Check them only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly as part of your normal scanning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often for your safety. It is important to know what is behind you. Make mirror checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: What gives you the most helmet protection?

options.text: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that has been in a previous crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for maximum protection. Your helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: Should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: No, they will make your hands too hot.
Yes, they give you a better grip on the handlebars.
No, they make it harder to work the controls.
Yes, but only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear gloves made of leather or another durable material. They give you a better grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face just as well as a face shield.
Your face the same way a windshield does.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not provide enough protection on its own.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve visibility?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Always use your headlight, signals, and brake light properly.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Squeeze the tire to feel it.

questions.explanation: Check your tire pressure with a tire gauge before every ride. A tire that is low on air may still look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is around to see it.

questions.question: How can you reduce head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual gives you specific information about your bike.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to a row of parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be going slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver may pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes provide the best protection for riding?

options.text: Long laces that are not tucked in.
High enough to cover the ankle with good support.

questions.correctAnswerText: High enough to cover the ankle with good support.
questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one spot in the lane, limiting your movement.
It lets you rely on others to find hazards.
It requires you to go faster to stay with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. A small mechanical problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous on the road.

questions.question: When it is clear you are going to turn, should you use a turn signal?

options.text: No, you do not need to use a turn signal.
Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if it seems obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you don't see.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist continually scan the road ahead for?
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react to anything that changes.

questions.question: If your footwear has laces, what should you do with them?
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely when riding so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to eliminate alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on which surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal road covers are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that:
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips
Should be part of your normal scanning routine
Are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently as part of your normal routine. Always check mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal road covers are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.
